findings.measured: Overall L/R correlation is -0.78; likely a polarity problem.

steps.text: The whole mix is out of polarity between left and right. Check the master and bus inserts, and the output routing, for a flip on one side.
Insert Trim as multi-mono on the stereo track and click Ø on one side only.

findings.measured: Below 150 Hz the correlation is -0.78; bass and kick may thin out in mono.

steps.text: Insert F6 in M/S mode and cut the Side below 150 Hz with a high-pass band.

other_options.text: Check the kick and bass tracks for chorus, wideners or stereo patches.

findings.measured: The mix loses 9.6 dB when summed to mono.

steps.text: Sum the master to mono and listen for parts that disappear.
Reduce stereo widening (chorus, doublers, wideners, very short stereo delays) on the tracks that vanish in mono.
Solo tracks between 0:00 and 0:40 to find the source. Usual suspects: stereo wideners, a very short delay on one side, a stereo bass patch, or double-miked sources.
Insert Trim as multi-mono on the stereo track and click Ø on one side only.

other_options.text: Watch a correlation meter while you loop 0:00–0:40; it should stay above 0.
Select the whole clip and run AudioSuite › Other › Invert.

notes.headline: One side of this mix is polarity-flipped — L/R correlation is -0.78 for the full 0:40, and everything else in the report follows from that.
notes.summary: Your levels and headroom are fine for a mix going to mastering, but the stereo image is inverted: correlation sits at -0.78 across the whole file, -0.777 below 150 Hz, and the mix loses 9.6 dB when summed to mono. That's a polarity flip on one channel, not a width choice — on any mono playback the mix will largely cancel. Find and undo the flip first, then re-check the low end and mono sum; the score goes from 6.5 to 10.0 once that's handled.

judge.priority_order: Polarity flip (critical, F1/F4) is placed first before the low-end check (F2, critical) - though F2 is technically also critical, grouping F1/F4/F3 as the dominant cause is reasonable and matches severity ordering.
judge.explains_impact: Priority 1 explains mono cancellation on club subs/phones/broadcast, and priority 2 explains bass/kick thinning in mono.
judge.groups_causes: F1, F4, and F3 are grouped as stemming from the same polarity flip, while F2 (low-end specific) is kept separate, matching the report's shared correlation values.
judge.specific: Notes cite exact measurements like -0.78 correlation, -0.777 below 150Hz, 9.6dB mono loss, and the 0:00-0:40 timeframe specific to this bounce.
judge.stage_appropriate: Notes correctly state levels/headroom are fine for mastering and don't judge loudness as a master would be judged.
judge.faithful: The notes claim 'if not, the bass has its own width problem' and imply mono loss issue is separate/could be independent from polarity, but F2 in the report explicitly attributes the low-end issue to the same overall correlation problem (-0.78), and the report doesn't support a claim of a second independent bass width problem beyond what's already covered by F1/F4.
judge.concise: The notes are structured and avoid excessive repetition or filler, staying focused on the polarity issue and its consequences.
